message.content: The sea usually appears **blue**—the water itself scatters sunlight, especially shorter‑wave (blue) wavelengths—but its hue can shift dramatically based on depth, weather, time of day, algae or sediment content, and even nearby land colors. So while “sea” often conjures images of deep azure, it’s really a spectrum ranging from pale turquoise near shorelines to dark indigo in deeper waters.
